questions.question: How is data organized in ServiceNow?

options.text: Files, folders, and documents
Tables, records, fields, and values
Sheets, cells, and formulas
Objects, classes, and methods

explanation.correct: In ServiceNow, data is organized in a database with tables, records, fields, and values. Tables store records, records contain fields, fields hold individual pieces of data, and values are accessed through fields and records. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=f798635447735ad4ca332a81736d4382&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: ServiceNow uses a relational database structure, not a file system.
These are spreadsheet concepts, not ServiceNow's data structure.
While ServiceNow uses object-oriented concepts, data is stored in tables.

source.excerpt: In ServiceNow, data is organized in a database with tables, records, fields, and values.

questions.question: What is a sys_id in ServiceNow?

options.text: A user's login name
A unique 32-character ID that identifies each record
The table name
A field label

explanation.correct: Records have a unique 32-character ID called a sys_id. This identifier is automatically generated and uniquely identifies each record in the database. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=f798635447735ad4ca332a81736d4382&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: User login names are stored in the user_name field, not sys_id.
Table names are separate from record identifiers.
Field labels are display names, not unique record identifiers.

source.excerpt: Records have a unique 32-character ID called a sys_id.

questions.question: What does a reference field store in ServiceNow?

options.text: The full content of the referenced record
The unique sys_id of a record from another table
A copy of the referenced table
The URL of an external system

explanation.correct: A reference field stores the unique sys_id of a record from another table, creating a link between them. This link makes fields from the reference table accessible in the form. Reference fields only connect to one table. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=f798635447735ad4ca332a81736d4382&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Reference fields store the sys_id, not the full record content.
Tables are not copied; only a reference link is created.
External URLs are stored differently; reference fields link internal records.

source.excerpt: A reference field stores the unique sys_id of a record from another table, creating a link between them.

questions.question: What happens when a table extends another table in ServiceNow?

options.text: The parent table is deleted
The child table inherits all fields from its parent table along with its unique fields
Both tables become identical
The parent table can no longer be used

explanation.correct: An extended table inherits all fields from its parent table along with its unique fields. When extending a table, all fields and properties from the parent table are inherited, while unique fields can be added to the child table. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=f798635447735ad4ca332a81736d4382&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: The parent table remains intact; extension creates a relationship.
Child tables have additional unique fields beyond inherited ones.
Parent tables remain fully functional after extension.

source.excerpt: An extended table inherits all fields from its parent table along with its unique fields.

questions.question: Which of the following are examples of tables that extend the Task table?

options.text: User and Group
Incident, Problem, and Change Request
Location and Department
Knowledge and Article

explanation.correct: Examples of parent tables in ServiceNow include the Task and Configuration Item tables, which are extended to create child classes like change, request, incident, and problem. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=f798635447735ad4ca332a81736d4382&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: User and Group are separate tables, not extensions of Task.
Location and Department are reference tables, not Task extensions.
Knowledge tables extend different parent tables.

source.excerpt: Examples of parent tables in ServiceNow include the Task and Configuration Item tables, which are extended to create child classes, like change, request, incident, and problem.

questions.question: What is a base table in ServiceNow?

options.text: A table that has been deleted
A table that serves as a foundation for other tables but isn't an extension itself
A temporary table for testing
A table that cannot have child tables

explanation.correct: A base table serves as a foundation for other tables but isn't an extension itself. A parent table without a parent is a base class. It can also be a parent and/or core table. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=f798635447735ad4ca332a81736d4382&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Base tables are active tables, not deleted ones.
Base tables are permanent production tables, not temporary.
Base tables can have child tables; that's often their purpose.

source.excerpt: Base table serves as a foundation for other tables, but isn't an extension itself.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a Schema Map in ServiceNow?

options.text: To display user permissions
To visualize table relationships
To track system performance
To manage email notifications

explanation.correct: The Schema Map visualizes table relationships. You can use the schema map to identify which columns originate on a table and which columns are inherited from parent tables, plus what tables are referenced. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=f798635447735ad4ca332a81736d4382&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: User permissions are managed in the security modules, not schema map.
System performance is tracked with different tools.
Notifications are managed in System Notification modules.

questions.question: What is the difference between a field name and a field label?

options.text: They are always identical
Field names are unique and may differ from labels, which are display names
Field labels are used in scripts; field names are for display
There is no difference

explanation.correct: Field names are unique and may differ from labels. For instance, 'city' is the field name in the sys_user table for the label 'Location'. Labels are display names shown to users. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=f798635447735ad4ca332a81736d4382&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Field names and labels often differ, as shown with city/Location example.
It's the opposite - field names are used in scripts, labels are for display.
There is a clear difference between technical names and display labels.

source.excerpt: Field names are unique and may differ from labels. For instance, city is the field name in the sys_user table for the label Location.

questions.question: What type of field allows selecting multiple records from a table?

options.text: Reference field
Choice field
GlideList field
String field

explanation.correct: GlideList allows selecting multiple records from a table. For example, the Watch List field on the Incident table can link to multiple User table records. Reference fields only allow selecting one record. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=f798635447735ad4ca332a81736d4382&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Reference fields allow selecting only one record from a specific table.
Choice fields provide predefined value options, not table record selections.
String fields hold text values, not record references.

source.excerpt: GlideList allows selecting multiple records from a table. Example, Watch List field on the Incident table can link to multiple User table records.

questions.question: What is the difference between scoped apps and global apps?

options.text: Scoped apps are free; global apps require licensing
Scoped apps are sandboxed with restricted API; global apps have access to all parts of the system
Global apps are more secure than scoped apps
There is no difference

explanation.correct: Scoped apps are sandboxed from the system at large and utilize a restricted API to minimize or prevent damage outside their scope. Global apps have access to all parts of the system and can cause damage/impact beyond their intent. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=f798635447735ad4ca332a81736d4382&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: The difference is about access scope, not licensing costs.
Scoped apps are more secure because they have restricted access.
There is a significant difference in system access and security.

source.excerpt: Scoped apps are sandboxed from the system at large and utilize a restricted API to minimize or prevent damage to anything outside of their scope.

questions.question: In the schema map, what do tables with blue bars indicate? (Choose two)

options.text: Tables that extend the focused table
Tables that are referenced by the focused table
Child tables of the focused table
Deleted tables

explanation.correct: In the schema map, tables with blue bars are tables that extend the focused table (child tables). Tables with red bars are tables that are referenced by the focused table. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=f798635447735ad4ca332a81736d4382&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Referenced tables are shown with red bars, not blue.
Deleted tables don't appear in the schema map.

source.excerpt: Tables with blue bars, including problem and change phase, are tables that extend the task table.

questions.question: What is a Document ID field used for?

options.text: To store document attachments
To reference one record from any table
To create PDF exports
To store version history

explanation.correct: Document ID fields allow selecting one record from any table, unlike reference fields which only connect to one specific table. Example: Document field in the Translated Text table. See: https://learning.servicenow.com/lxp/en/pages/learning-course?id=learning_course&course_id=400ce92b47530e10123f3975d36d43f1&child_id=f798635447735ad4ca332a81736d4382&spa=1

wrongAnswers.explanation: Attachments are stored differently, not through Document ID fields.
PDF exports are handled by reporting functions.
Version history is tracked separately.

source.excerpt: Document ID fields allows selecting one record from any table. Example, Document field in the Translated Text table.

questions.question: What is the unique identifier for every record in ServiceNow?

options.text: A record number (e.g., INC0010001)
A 32-character sys_id
A combination of table name and row number
An auto-generated UUID

explanation.correct: Every record in ServiceNow has a unique 32-character ID called a sys_id. Record numbers can auto-increment and their format can be changed, but the sys_id is the true unique identifier.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Record numbers like INC0010001 are display values that can be reformatted; the sys_id is the true unique identifier.
ServiceNow uses a 32-character sys_id, not a table name/row number combination.
While similar in concept, ServiceNow specifically uses a 32-character sys_id, not a standard UUID format.

questions.question: What is the difference between a base table and a core table in ServiceNow?

options.text: A base table is always a core table, but a core table is not always a base table
A base table serves as a foundation for extensions and is not itself an extension, while a core table comes with ServiceNow from the start
Base tables cannot have child tables, while core tables can
There is no difference; the terms are interchangeable

explanation.correct: A core table comes with ServiceNow (existing from the start) and can be a parent, child, or base table. A base table serves as a foundation for other tables but isn't itself an extension. A table can be both core and base.

wrongAnswers.explanation: A base table is not always a core table — custom tables can also be base tables.
Base tables can and often do have child tables — that's their primary purpose.
The terms have distinct meanings: core refers to origin (built-in), base refers to hierarchy (foundation).

questions.question: Which of the following are types of field relationships in ServiceNow? (Choose 2)

options.text: One-to-many (Reference field)
Many-to-many
One-to-one-to-many
Circular reference

explanation.correct: ServiceNow supports one-to-many relationships (using reference fields like Caller on Incident linking to User) and many-to-many relationships (connecting two or more tables so related records are visible in both, like students and classes).

wrongAnswers.explanation: One-to-one-to-many is not a standard relationship type in ServiceNow.
Circular reference is not a defined relationship type in ServiceNow's data model.

questions.question: What is the purpose of coalescing during a data import in ServiceNow?

options.text: To merge multiple import set tables into one
To prevent duplicate records by using fields as unique keys
To convert data types during transformation
To automatically map fields between source and target tables

explanation.correct: Coalesce prevents duplicate records during data import. It makes a field act as a unique key — if a match is found, the existing record is updated; if unmatched, a new record is created. Without coalescing, all imported rows are treated as new records.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Coalescing is about preventing duplicates in the target table, not merging import set tables.
Data type conversion is handled by the transform map, not coalescing.
Automatic field mapping is done by the mapping utility, not coalescing.

questions.question: What do update sets capture in ServiceNow?

options.text: Both configuration changes and data records like incidents
Only data records created during the update set period
Configuration and customization changes, but NOT data records
Only changes made by administrators with elevated privileges

explanation.correct: Update sets capture customization or configuration changes like report definitions, but not actual data records. New incidents or change records are not included. To move data records, use the Export XML function.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Update sets do NOT capture data records like incidents or change requests — only configuration changes.
Update sets capture configuration changes, not data records.
Update sets capture all configuration changes regardless of whether elevated privileges were used.

questions.question: What is the difference between global scope and application scope in ServiceNow?

options.text: Global scope is for production only; application scope is for development
Global scope has access to all parts of the system; scoped apps are sandboxed with restricted API access
Application scope provides more permissions than global scope
There is no functional difference between the two

explanation.correct: Scoped apps are sandboxed from the system at large and use a restricted API to minimize damage outside their scope. Global apps are the default scope and have access to all parts of the system, which means they can potentially cause impact beyond their intent.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Both scopes can be used in any instance type, not limited to production or development.
Global scope has broader access; application scope is intentionally restricted.
There is a significant functional difference in access and security between the two.

questions.question: An administrator needs to import 5,000 user records from a CSV file. After the import, several records have incorrect department values. Which step in the import process most likely caused this issue?

options.text: The Transform Map field mapping for Department used an incorrect coalesce field
The CSV file was too large to process
The import set table was not created
The user running the import lacked the admin role

explanation.correct: When reference field mappings (like Department) use incorrect coalesce fields in the Transform Map, records may map to wrong values or create duplicates. The coalesce field determines how imported values match existing reference records.

wrongAnswers.explanation: ServiceNow handles large CSV imports; 5,000 records is well within limits.
If the import set table wasn't created, the import would fail entirely, not produce incorrect values.
The import_admin or admin role is needed to run imports, but role issues would prevent the import, not cause incorrect mappings.

questions.question: Which two field types in ServiceNow store references to records in other tables? (Choose 2)

options.text: Reference field
Glide List field
String field
Integer field

explanation.correct: Reference fields store a single reference (sys_id) to a record in another table. Glide List fields store multiple references (comma-separated sys_ids) to records in another table.

wrongAnswers.explanation: String fields store plain text values, not record references.
Integer fields store numeric values, not references to other records.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a 'coalesce' field in a Transform Map?

options.text: It determines whether to update an existing record or insert a new one during import
It combines multiple source columns into one target field
It encrypts sensitive data during import
It validates data format before insertion

explanation.correct: A coalesce field acts as a unique identifier during data import. If a record with a matching coalesce value exists, it's updated; if not, a new record is inserted. This prevents duplicate records during imports.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Combining columns is done through field mapping scripts, not coalescing.
Data encryption is handled by encryption contexts, not coalesce fields.
Data validation can be done through transform scripts, not the coalesce setting itself.

questions.question: An administrator wants to create a field that automatically calculates the number of days between the Opened date and the Resolved date on an incident. Which field type is most appropriate?

options.text: Duration field with a calculated default value
Integer field with a Business Rule to calculate the value
Formula field that references the two date fields
String field with a UI Policy to display the calculation

explanation.correct: An Integer field populated by a Business Rule (before insert/update) that calculates the day difference between opened_at and resolved_at is the most reliable approach. Business Rules ensure the value is always accurate when the record is saved.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Duration fields store time spans but calculated default values only run on record creation, not on updates.
ServiceNow doesn't have a 'Formula field' type in the standard platform.
UI Policies control form display behavior; they don't calculate and store values in the database.

questions.question: What is the maximum number of rows that can be displayed in a single list view by default in ServiceNow?

options.text: Unlimited

explanation.correct: By default, ServiceNow displays 20 rows per page in list views. This can be changed by the user (up to the system maximum) or by an administrator through the glide.ui.per_page system property.

wrongAnswers.explanation: 100 rows can be configured but is not the default setting.
500 is not the default; displaying this many rows would impact performance.
Lists always paginate; there is no unlimited display option by default.

questions.question: Which statement about table inheritance in ServiceNow is correct?

options.text: Child tables inherit all fields and business logic from their parent table
Child tables share the same physical database table but cannot have additional fields
Parent table records are automatically duplicated in child tables
Table inheritance only works with the Task table

explanation.correct: In ServiceNow's table inheritance model, child tables (extensions) inherit all parent fields, ACLs, business rules, and other configurations. Child tables can also define additional fields specific to their needs.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Child tables CAN have additional fields beyond what the parent defines.
Records exist in one table; they are not duplicated across parent and child tables.
While Task is the most common example, any table can be extended to create inheritance hierarchies.
